captions.absence-of-evidence-fallacy: A man in a suit examines audit reports with a magnifying glass while another man gestures confidently toward the empty space, and a thought bubble shows masked figures tampering with a voting machine. The visible elements suggest a careful search for wrongdoing, but the gesture and thought bubble indicate someone still infers a hidden conspiracy despite the lack of evidence found. The important contrast is between the thorough investigation with visible audit papers and magnifying glass, and the imagined conspiracy shown in the thought bubble. We can see that simply failing to find traces in the audit reports is treated as entirely irrelevant, but the visible absence of evidence does not by itself disprove—or prove—the existence of a hidden scheme that ought to have left signs.
captions.abstraction-denial: A worried family sits by a bag of groceries labeled with high prices and an upward graph, while a confident man in a suit gestures dismissively and points toward scenes of individual transactions, such as buying milk and purchasing a car. From these elements, the further claim being inferred is that broad economic problems like inflation do not exist as real harmful forces, but are merely collections of isolated trades between buyers and sellers. The important contrast is between the visible suffering and patterns shown in the family scene with the graph and the narrow focus on single transactions depicted elsewhere. We can see the emotional distress, recognizable price tags, and clear pattern of rising costs, but these alone do not prove that inflation’s impact disappears just because all prices result from individual deals.
captions.abstraction-fallacy: On the left, a smiling man gestures confidently at a rising bar graph and a stack of computer servers, creating the impression of steady technological progress. On the right, a person crouches in distress beside a broken, smoking computer and a snail, suggesting that any slowdown or failure is impossible and somehow violates an unbreakable rule of advancement. The important contrast is between the visible evidence of past progress and malfunctioning equipment versus the inferred claim that progress must always continue at the same rate, no matter what. We can see that the visible growth trend and optimism do not guarantee that setbacks, failures, or slowdowns cannot happen in reality.
captions.ad-hominem: A woman in professional clothing stands at a podium pointing to a chart, while a man in a suit leans forward angrily, pointing at her, and another man in work clothes laughs and cheers him on; prominent symbols like a graduation cap, a university building, and books are visible near the man’s feet. The scene suggests that the woman’s education or background is being used as a reason to dismiss whatever point she is making about tariff costs. The important contrast is between the woman visibly presenting information or evidence and the man attacking her personal background instead of addressing her argument. We can see that the chart and her presentation provide content for discussion, but the visible hostility and reference to her education do not by themselves disprove her argument or make her data invalid.
captions.affirmative-conclusion-from-a-negative-p: A man holds a paper marked "source" and gestures confidently toward a shadowy figure with a question mark for a face, while two onlookers watch and a large stack of approved documents sits nearby. The situation implies that, because their source is not anonymous like the mysterious figure labeled "unreliable," it must be completely reliable and trustworthy. The important contrast is between the visible relief and approval of the people with their stack of checked documents and the inferred certainty about the quality of the source. We can see that simply not being anonymous doesn’t by itself prove that the source is reliable, since none of the papers or actions shown provide any actual evidence of trustworthiness.
captions.affirming-a-disjunct: The image shows two men, one angrily pointing and the other looking surprised with raised hands, a large red X, and a television displaying edited film strips and a man holding a money bag. The situation suggests that because the video has been edited, it cannot also be misleading, as if these are the only two options and one excludes the other. The important contrast is between the visible evidence of editing—film strips, scissors, the word "edited"—and the inferred claim that editing alone rules out the possibility of deception. We can see the video has been physically altered, but nothing about the scene proves that the edited content cannot also be misleading.
captions.affirming-the-consequent: A TV screen displays warped, distorted hands while two people energetically point at the screen and another person works at a control desk with film reels and editing equipment. Observers seem to claim that because the video shows unnatural hands, it must have been created by artificial intelligence. The important contrast is between the visible evidence of warped hands and excited discussion, and the inferred conclusion that AI is the only possible cause for the video. We can see that the scene presents only a specific visual flaw, but does not rule out other explanations like editing mistakes or technical errors in the film.
captions.all-or-nothing-fallacy: A man points angrily at two worried people while another hand throws a stack of reports marked "REPORT" into a trash can full of flames; a magnifying glass and scattered papers are visible on a nearby desk. The visible error being circled and criticized is being treated as a reason to discard the entire set of documents, as if one mistake ruins the full report beyond use. The important contrast is between the single marked mistake shown and the total rejection of all the work symbolized by burning every report. We can see that discovering one flaw does not prove that everything in the report is worthless or should be destroyed, since most pages are left unread and unchecked.
captions.anecdotal-fallacy: A smiling older man with a cigarette and a photograph is seated on one side of a balance scale, while a large stack of studies, a medical image of lungs, and charts are piled on the opposite side; below, a person points to the scale while speaking to a skeptical companion. The immediate impression is that one person’s story or example about a smoker who lived long and enjoyed life is being weighed directly against mountains of scientific evidence and research. The important contrast is between the vivid, personal image and anecdote on one side, and the broad, rigorous collection of scientific studies on the other. We can see that a single photograph and personal story do not, by themselves, outweigh or disprove the findings from systematic research and medical data.
captions.appeal-to-accomplishment: A woman stands confidently at a podium under a spotlight, holding a test tube and a folder, with a tall building marked “Tech Corp” and an upward-pointing stock chart behind her. Nearby, a pair of older people examine a book with food illustrations and a bottle with a medical cross, as large icons of an apple, pills, and a DNA strand hover above them, suggesting health or scientific authority. The important contrast is between the woman’s visible success in the technology business world and the audience’s assumption that this success justifies conclusions about nutrition or medicine. We can see impressive business symbols and attentive listeners, but these details do not by themselves demonstrate any expertise or evidence about health and aging.
captions.appeal-to-authority: The image shows a smiling man in medical attire speaking into a microphone, a happy woman presenting a bottle labeled "Super Supplements," a pair of silhouettes in lab coats arguing with check marks beside them, and a cheering couple giving a thumbs-up. The further claim being inferred is that the supplement must be effective and trustworthy simply because an authority figure, such as a doctor or expert, is seen endorsing it. The important contrast is between the visible excitement, authoritative appearance, and symbolic check marks, versus the actual evidence needed to prove the supplement’s effectiveness. We can see endorsements and approval gestures, but these alone do not provide real scientific proof that the product works.
captions.appeal-to-consequences: The image shows a man in a suit holding money and raising his hand to refuse, with cars, a golf bag, and factory smokestacks behind him, while on the other side a scientist urgently points to a flaming thermometer under a melting earth, next to a shocked woman. The situation implies that because acting on climate change would be expensive or disruptive, warnings about the problem must not be true or must be exaggerated. The important contrast is between the visible discomfort at potential costs and the inferred claim that these costs mean the scientific danger is false or overstated. We can see that concern about money, cars, and industry does not by itself give evidence about the reality or severity of the warming shown by the thermometer and globe.
captions.appeal-to-emotion: A man at a podium gestures forcefully while holding up a picture of two crying children, with papers filled with data and graphs discarded in a trash can nearby. From these elements, the implied claim is that the emotional distress shown in the children is the main or only valid reason to make a decision, outweighing any evidence or argument presented in the documents. The important contrast is between the vivid, emotional image being displayed and the ignored, concrete records and reports thrown away. We can see that the visible appeals to emotion do not, by themselves, demonstrate that the emotional response is the strongest or most logical basis for making a decision.
captions.appeal-to-fear: A man in a suit stands at a podium, gesturing sharply and speaking with an angry, urgent expression, while nearby, a masked figure holds a bomb and an explosion devastates a city in the background; below, two people look up in terror. From these dramatic scenes, the image infers that passing a certain bill is the only way to prevent disastrous violence and destruction by unseen attackers. The important contrast is between the visible elements of fear—explosions, threatening gestures, anxious faces—and the inferred claim that this particular action will entirely determine safety from disaster. We can see people looking frightened and a politician making intense warnings, but those images alone do not actually prove that passing the bill will prevent any specific threat from happening.
captions.appeal-to-flattery: A man in a suit is smiling and gesturing toward two attentive people, with a glowing lightbulb labeled "flattery" prominently displayed between them and a wastebasket full of crumpled papers marked "facts." The immediate impression is that the man is using charm and praise to win approval, rather than offering evidence, as the people respond with pleased and thoughtful expressions. The important contrast is between the visible encouragement and admiration the people are shown, and the unseen implication that their agreement proves they are right or especially insightful. We can see friendly gestures and discarded evidence, but these alone do not demonstrate the truth or falsehood of the speaker’s claim.
captions.appeal-to-motive: A woman stands at a podium presenting a study, while two men whisper and smirk to each other, pointing toward her and a table stacked with money and a sack marked with a dollar sign. This creates the impression that the woman's research is being influenced or controlled by unseen financial support from landlords represented by distant buildings. The important contrast is between the visible scene of a person sharing research results and the inferred idea that her work must be untrustworthy because of supposed hidden motives tied to money. We can see the podium, the money, and the gestures, but these alone do not prove that her research findings are false or corrupt.
captions.appeal-to-nature: The image shows a cheerful woman presenting a bottle labeled with leaves in a sunny, natural setting, while a worried man in a lab coat stands beside prescription bottles and pills under a skull-and-crossbones symbol. The scene visually suggests that the "natural" remedy is good and safe, while the "unnatural" medicine is harmful or deadly. The important contrast is between the appealing, peaceful imagery of nature and the dark, alarming imagery surrounding the prescription drugs. We can see plants, animals, and sunshine versus pills, a skull, and worry, but these visible cues alone do not actually prove anything about which remedy is safer or more effective.
captions.appeal-to-novelty: The image shows a classroom split into two scenes: on the left, an older teacher with a chalkboard and globe, and on the right, a modern instructor with a robot, laptops, headset-wearing students, and a rocket launch poster. The arrangement suggests that the new high-tech classroom is automatically superior to the traditional setting simply because it features futuristic elements. The important contrast is between the clear, visual presence of new technology and enthusiasm on one side and the suggested conclusion that these qualities guarantee better teaching or learning. We can see that the props and excitement alone do not actually demonstrate which method is better or more effective—only that one is newer and more visually dynamic than the other.
captions.appeal-to-pity: A teary-eyed student clasps his hands in a pleading gesture across from a stern-looking teacher, with a failed test paper on the desk between them. Above the student, a thought bubble shows a distressed family, and between them another bubble shows an empty wallet and loose coins. The important contrast is between the student’s visible sadness and desperate appeal and the unstated claim that the teacher should pass him simply because of his difficult situation. We can see that the visible evidence of hardship and emotion does not actually address whether the student deserves to pass the test.
captions.appeal-to-poverty: A man in tattered clothes stands on a crate above two well-dressed men, one holding charts and the other clutching stacks of papers, while the man on the crate gestures confidently. The scene suggests that because the central figure appears poor and rough, his advice or analysis is presumed to be wiser or more trustworthy than that of the businessmen below him, despite their professional materials. The important contrast is between the visible poverty and humble appearance of the speaker, and the inferred idea that this alone guarantees wisdom or deeper insight. We can see that his background, attire, and posture do not by themselves prove his opinions are more valid than those of others with research or expertise.
captions.appeal-to-probability: A smiling person in a suit is shown eagerly throwing money at three computer screens with upward-trending rocket charts, while a dream bubble shows them relaxing on a tropical beach. The image infers that investing in these stocks will inevitably lead to great wealth and a carefree lifestyle, as suggested by the pot of gold and the dream bubble. The important contrast is between the visible hopeful actions—pouring money into the screens, a broken piggy bank, and the fantasy of instant riches—and the mere possibility of getting rich rather than certainty. We can see the enthusiastic investment and wishful thinking, but nothing in the scene demonstrates that this strategy guarantees success or wealth.
captions.appeal-to-ridicule: Two people are laughing and pointing at a person who sits inside a makeshift bunker made of tinfoil, wearing a tinfoil hat, with a computer in front of them. The scene suggests that the person in the bunker is being mocked simply for caring about privacy or security, implying their concerns are absurd or paranoid. The important contrast is between the visible elements of ridicule—pointing fingers, exaggerated laughter, and tinfoil props—and the inference that being concerned about privacy is foolish or unworthy of serious consideration. We can see that mockery and exaggerated gestures alone do not actually address or disprove the person’s concerns about privacy.
captions.appeal-to-spite: The image shows two people with angry expressions holding a paper labeled “BILLS” on one side, while on the other, a group of graduates in caps and gowns are celebrating with diplomas and glasses. The immediate situation suggests resentment from the first group as they look toward the celebrating graduates, with a large document about “DEBT” shown between them on stacks of books. The further inference being pushed is that the resentment or bitterness of the bill-paying group justifies rejecting relief for the debt held by the graduates. The important contrast is between the visible emotions of anger and joy versus the suggested conclusion that negative feelings alone determine what should happen about debt. We can see frustration and celebration, but these emotions do not by themselves prove what policy should be chosen or what is fair regarding student debt.
captions.appeal-to-tradition: A stern man in a suit stands on stage holding a flaming torch and pointing emphatically, while a musician in old-fashioned parade attire plays a drum and trumpet nearby; an audience and two nervous young presenters holding papers watch. This scene suggests that because a ceremonial tradition with specific props and costumes has been followed year after year, it must be the correct or only way to proceed, pushing aside consideration of the new program. The important contrast is between the visible routine and pageantry on stage—costumes, torch, drum, and an old photograph—and the inferred belief that tradition alone guarantees rightness or superiority. We can see people enacting a familiar custom, but this repetition does not by itself show that no improvement or change could be better.
captions.appeal-to-wealth: A man in a suit stands at a podium holding a large bag marked with a dollar sign, flanked by stacks of cash, while an enthusiastic crowd points toward him and a doctor and nurse look on uncertainly beside a crossed-out health policy chart. The scene suggests that the speaker’s wealth and business success imply he is especially qualified to decide on matters of health policy. The important contrast is between the visible signs of financial success, like the money bags and happy audience, and the assumption that this success guarantees expertise in a completely different field. We can see that having money or popularity does not by itself prove someone is knowledgeable or correct about complex medical decisions.
captions.argument-from-fallacy: A woman holds a chart marked “false statistics” while two people watch, one pointing and laughing, and below, there is a street scene with a “no vacancy” sign and a person huddled by a fire. The further claim being inferred is that since the statistics about housing were false, the entire problem of people lacking housing—and possibly the housing crisis itself—must also be false or made up. The important contrast is between the visible exposure of a faulty argument or error in data and the much broader, unseen conclusion that the underlying social problem does not exist. We can see the visible evidence of someone suffering on the street, which shows that discovering errors in argument does not by itself disprove the reality of homelessness or housing shortages.
captions.argument-from-ignorance: A smiling man holds up a paper labeled “secret memo” while another person looks worried near a bulletin board with a large question mark, and a woman examines documents labeled as evidence with a magnifying glass. The scene creates the impression that, because nobody has disproved the memo’s authenticity, it is being declared real without further investigation. The important contrast is between the visible uncertainty and careful searching for clues, and the bold assumption that the memo must be genuine simply due to a lack of disproof. We can see that not finding solid evidence or disproof does not by itself confirm the memo’s authenticity without actual supporting facts.
captions.argument-from-incredulity: The image shows a worried man in a suit pointing toward a glowing spirit with a halo, while behind him, a brain sits under a microscope and a scientist gestures to gears and lightning inside another man’s head. From these elements, the scene infers that because the man cannot understand how the brain works using science alone, he concludes a supernatural soul must exist. The important contrast is between the physical objects and scientific symbols, which are visible and concrete, and the glowing spirit figure, which is an imagined cause based on confusion or disbelief. We can see confusion and symbols of science, but nothing in the visible scene by itself proves the existence of a supernatural being or soul.
captions.argument-from-repetition: A man at a podium shouts through a megaphone, surrounded by large signs repeating the same phrase, while a distressed woman and a confused man look on and a conveyor belt delivers even more identical signs. The repeated signs and the emotional reactions suggest that the claim being shouted is becoming more convincing or true simply because it is heard so often. The important contrast is between the visible flood of repeated messages and the unproven accusation they are meant to reinforce. We can see that simple repetition and emotional display do not provide actual proof, as shown by the ignored documents and magnifying glass labeled “facts” on the table.
captions.argument-from-silence: A man in the foreground energetically holds up a paper labeled “Scandal Claim,” while three serious-looking people sit silently in the background near a “No Response” sign and a clock showing time passing. The implication is that the lack of any reaction or denial from the silent group is being used to infer that the scandal claim must be true. The important contrast is between the visible silence and inaction of the group and the much larger conclusion of guilt that the man is drawing from it. We can see only quiet people and discarded papers in a tense setting, but this does not by itself prove that the accusation is correct or that any scandal actually occurred.
captions.argumentum-ad-baculum: A stern-looking man stands behind a podium, pointing and gripping a large lever marked with a warning symbol, while another man stands nearby sweating and raising his hands anxiously. This scene suggests that the anxious man’s agreement is being forced by the threat of some consequence if he does not comply, rather than reached through discussion or evidence. The important contrast is between the visible threat and fear on one side, and the idea of a fair balance of reasons on the other, as shown by the unconsidered scales in the foreground. We can see that intimidation and the potential for punishment, not actual reasons or evidence, are causing the agreement, so the truth of any claim remains unsupported.
captions.argumentum-ad-populum: A crowd of enthusiastic people is raising phones and signs with thumbs-up symbols, while a man is proudly presenting a bottle labeled "Miracle Detox" and a woman displays a phone showing a large number of likes; meanwhile, a skeptical scientist stands near a microscope beside a bin filled with discarded papers. This lively display suggests that because so many people approve of or promote the detox bottle, it must be effective or scientifically valid. The important contrast is between the visible popularity and excitement of the crowd and the unproven value or truth of the detox product they support. We can see many people expressing approval, but their excitement alone does not provide any genuine evidence that the "Miracle Detox" works as claimed.
captions.artificial-negation: A man shrugs with uncertain facial expression, thinking about a cartoon ghost, while another person aggressively points at him and slams a folder with a big red X onto the table; a woman stands by holding a clipboard labeled with a question mark. From this scene, it is inferred that simply not knowing if ghosts exist is treated as the same as making a strong claim that ghosts definitely do not exist, with the demand to "prove" this denial. The important contrast is between the visible uncertainty and open question on one side, and the forced leap to a definite, positive denial of ghosts on the other. We can see uncertainty, questioning, and a lack of evidence—but nothing in the visible scene justifies treating doubt or nonbelief as an active claim against the existence of ghosts.
captions.association-fallacy: The image shows an angry man pointing at a woman near a sign for an affordable housing plan, while a thought bubble above them contains two men in dark glasses holding a bag of money and a laptop, set against a cityscape. This scene implies that the housing proposal is suspicious or corrupt simply because it is associated with wealthy city figures. The important contrast is between the visible discussion about housing and the imagined connection to shady characters with money. We can see the discussion and the angry gestures, but nothing in the visible scene actually proves that the housing plan is corrupt or controlled by those figures.
captions.bare-assertion-fallacy: A man in a suit stands at the center, gesturing forcefully and shouting, while another person examines papers with a magnifying glass and a woman holds up a clipboard with charts. The immediate situation suggests a heated debate over documents and reports, with the central figure confidently pointing and making a bold claim. The further claim being inferred is that the jobs report is definitely manipulated by hidden forces, presented as an obvious truth that needs no proof. The important contrast is between the physical scene of paperwork, charts, and examination tools, and the sweeping accusation of rigging that is simply asserted. We can see stacks of documents, analytic gestures, and visual references to evidence, but no specific proof is given to actually support the claim of manipulation.
captions.base-rate-fallacy: A worried man holds up an alert sign, imagining a masked thief holding a flashlight and a money bag, while another man with a clipboard points to bar graphs and a crowd of people under a magnifying glass. From the alert and the frightened expression, the immediate impression is that a nearby crime has almost certainly been discovered. The important contrast is between the vivid signal from the alert and the imagined thief, and the more measured analysis shown by bar graphs and groups representing larger numbers. We can see that the alarming scene alone does not prove that actual fraud has occurred, since the graphs and population suggest false alarms are common and context matters.
captions.begging-the-question: The image shows two people in suits pointing at signs above each other’s heads while curved arrows loop their claims back into one another. The further claim being inferred is that each person’s trustworthiness is proved by the other’s say-so, so the circle itself is treated as evidence. The important contrast is between the visible loop of mutual endorsement and the missing outside support that would actually justify either claim. We can see each person backing the other, but that does not by itself prove that either one is truthful or reliable.
captions.bottom-up-condemnation: A sharply dressed man holds a bag of money and a document labeled “Cuts,” while two worried people sit nearby at a table with a broken piggy bank, scattered coins, and a teddy bear. The scene suggests that this man is immediately responsible for harming a community program for the sake of profit, simply because he appears wealthy and confident. The important contrast is between the visible evidence—money, broken savings, anxious faces, and the props of community service—and the inferred conclusion that this specific individual will inevitably act in a destructive, greedy way. We can see that the man’s profession and appearance alone do not prove his intentions or personal responsibility for eliminating the program.
captions.bottom-up-justification: A smiling nurse in uniform stands beside a man giving a thumbs up, next to a sign showing a medical charity, while a thought bubble shows the same nurse accepting cash from a masked man and discarding a report in the trash. The visible approval and symbols of charity create the clear impression that the nurse should be trusted and her character admired, but the inset image suggests a hidden conclusion that her virtue or honesty can be guaranteed just because she belongs to a respected group. The important contrast is between the nurse’s outward role in a reputable organization and the inferred claim about her personal character and incorruptibility. We can see cheerful faces, uniforms, and charity symbols, but these alone do not provide evidence about the nurse's true actions or her moral qualities.
captions.broken-window-fallacy: The image shows a destroyed boardwalk, a closed shop, a worried bystander, happy workers repairing a building, smiling men exchanging money, a sad piggy bank, and a stack of cash. From these scenes, the further claim is being made that the destruction and repairs have created new economic benefits, as if damage and rebuilding lead to more wealth overall. The important contrast is between the visible repair activity and cash, which look positive, and the unseen losses implied by the closed shop and the sad piggy bank left behind. We can see the immediate repairs and spending, but these do not by themselves prove that the overall community is better off than before the destruction happened.
captions.cherry-picking: A man in a suit is holding up a single cherry and smiling next to a basket of cherries, while pointing at a chart with an upward arrow and a “good news” sign. The scene suggests he is using this single detail to claim that the overall economic situation is improving, despite other evidence. The important contrast is between the cheerful focus on one cherry and one upward chart, versus the visible struggles of worried people holding signs about high bills, low wages, and rising costs. We can see that showing only the positive chart and ignoring the unhappy faces, bills, and cost increases does not actually prove that things are good overall.
captions.chronological-snobbery: An elderly man in ancient robes holding a scroll stands beside a broken statue and a bust, while two modern people gesture dismissively, and a trash can displays discarded books, a scroll, and a head resembling the ancient man. Their confident gestures and the act of tossing old objects into the trash create the impression that ideas from the past are inherently worthless or irrelevant. The important contrast is between the visible presence of old artifacts and figures—which symbolize historical knowledge—and the leap to dismissing their value solely due to their age. We can see people throwing away books and symbols of the past, but this action alone does not prove that older ideas are automatically invalid or useless.
captions.circular-cause-and-consequence: A man angrily points at a phone displaying an app, a bored young man sits at a table, and empty chairs with a declining chart are shown, creating a scene of blame and disappointment. From these elements, the further claim being inferred is that the app is fated to be unpopular simply because it has no users, and it has no users because it is unpopular—a self-reinforcing causal loop treated as an explanation. The important contrast is between the visible cycle of frustration, empty chairs, and dropping chart, and the implied idea that these facts alone fully explain and justify the app’s failure. We can see a loop of low interest and participation, but the scene does not prove that this cycle is unavoidable or that other causes or solutions do not exist.
captions.composition-fallacy: On the left, scientists smile and give thumbs up next to checked-off robot parts, including a battery, a screen, and a camera, giving the impression that everything is in good order. On the right, the assembled robot lies broken and sparking on the floor, while the scientists appear shocked and panicked, suggesting an expectation that the robot should work perfectly since its parts were fine. The important contrast is between the individually approved components and the failed, malfunctioning robot as a whole. We can see that confirming each part works does not by itself prove that the completed robot will function properly.
captions.confidence-as-a-validator: A man stands confidently with a hand on his chest, shouting and pointing, while a large glowing sign labeled "gut feeling" dominates the center and other figures hold scientific equipment, a clipboard, or a magnifying glass. From this scene, the claim being inferred is that the man's powerful confidence and inner feeling are enough to prove his case, overriding the need for evidence or facts. The important contrast is between the man's visible show of certainty and emotion, and the unseen but implied truth or validity of his claim. We can see the outward display of confidence and dramatic gestures, but these visible cues alone do not demonstrate that the claim is actually supported by facts or evidence.
captions.conjunction-fallacy: A woman holding a protest sign with factory smokestacks and a carrot stands in front of two men, who observe two posters—one showing only the factory and the other showing the factory together with a carrot and a leaf. This scene suggests the observers are deciding it is more likely the woman is both concerned about pollution and also a supporter of plant-based diets, rather than just being concerned about pollution alone. The important contrast is between the simple, visible evidence of the woman’s environmental concern and the more detailed, combined story inferred by the onlookers. We can see the carrot and the sign, but nothing about their presence by itself proves that this more detailed and specific scenario is more probable than the simpler one.
captions.contextomy: The image shows a worried-looking scientist in a lab coat standing beside laboratory flasks, with a large pair of scissors cutting a strip of paper labeled “uncertain” and two excited men on the other side speaking into a microphone and holding a dramatic sign. The scene suggests that the scientist’s cautious statement is being taken and used by the other figures to claim that his scientific theory is collapsing or that science itself has failed. The important contrast is between the scientist’s visible uncertainty and responsible expression, and the sensational accusations and conclusions made by the two men, who are acting as reporters or critics. We can see only that the scientist expressed doubt or limitation, but nothing in the scene shows his theory is truly collapsing or that science is failing as claimed by the others.
captions.continuum-fallacy: A smiling man in a suit stands by a large, cheerful sales poster, while an angry man points forcefully toward a hesitant woman across a faded area between two labeled zones. The immediate impression is a heated argument about whether something being advertised is completely truthful or a flat-out lie, based on the placement of people near the words "TRUTH" and "LIES," with a blurry border between them. The important contrast is between the clear visual division of the "truth" and "lies" areas and the indistinct, smudged zone in the middle where the argument takes place. We can see that the visible fading and uncertainty in the boundary do not provide any evidence that nothing can be called true or false simply because the line between them is not perfectly clear.
captions.correlation-is-not-causation: A cheerful man points excitedly at a graph showing a sharp upward arrow, while a smiling woman stands beside him and a robot labeled "A.I. Tutor" beams in the background; meanwhile, at the bottom, a student works at a desk with a tutor and stacks of books. Their gestures, the rising arrow, and the beaming robot suggest the claim that the robot directly caused the improvement in results. The important contrast is between the visible evidence of increased scores and the presence of the A.I. tutor, versus the unseen cause that is simply assumed based on their coincidence. We can see an increase on the graph and the introduction of the robot, but nothing here proves that the robot alone caused the change, since other factors could have influenced the results.
captions.definist-fallacy: On the left side, a judge smiles and points at a paper marked "LEGAL," while on the right, a blindfolded woman holding unbalanced scales and a sword stands amid large question marks. This scene suggests that once something is declared legal by an authority, it should automatically be understood as completely just. The important contrast is between the clear visual of a confident judge with a legal document and the confused, uncertain figure of Justice pondering the connection. We can see that simply displaying a legal decision and authority does not, by itself, resolve deeper questions about fairness or justice.
captions.demanding-a-mechanism: Two smiling people in lab coats are pointing to a large board filled with stars arranged in a clear pattern, while a third person in a suit gestures angrily and holds a mess of gears and wires. The visible situation shows confident presenters displaying strong visual evidence for a pattern, while the man with gears demands to know the exact inner workings before accepting it as real. The important contrast is between the directly observable pattern of stars (evidence of a phenomenon) and the requirement for a detailed mechanical explanation before belief (requiring a hidden causal force or process to be revealed). We can see that the pattern’s reality is supported by the clear arrangement of stars on the board, but nothing about the visible scene requires a complete explanation of the machinery to accept the visible evidence.
captions.demanding-negative-proof: A man in a trench coat points dramatically at a folder labeled "Rigged Election," while another man in a suit, holding a magnifying glass, reacts with raised hands and a worried expression; behind them, a board with photos and red string suggests investigation, and there are separate images of a tired worker, a mover with equipment, and a pigeon near papers. From these elements, the claim is being inferred that a hidden force or conspiracy must be behind the election, unless every small event—like staff fatigue, moving equipment, and even a pigeon—is proven innocent beyond any doubt. The important contrast is between the visible minor incidents and the large, unseen accusation of election rigging. We can see that showing small, ordinary events with ambiguous meaning does not, on its own, justify concluding that a vast conspiracy actually exists.
captions.denial-of-the-epistemic-gradient: The image shows an angry man and woman on either side, each pointing forcefully at a large "YES" or "NO" box, with a confused person in a lab coat shrugging between them, and a robot with question marks above its head below. This scene suggests that only two extreme answers—absolute certainty or total impossibility—can be chosen about the robot’s consciousness, treating the matter as if there are no in-between states. The important contrast is between the dramatic, divided gestures and props above, which demand a binary choice, and the more nuanced visual below, where a question scale and uncertain robot hint at a spectrum of possible answers. We can see that the visible disagreement and props do not by themselves demonstrate that only absolute certainty or denial is justified, since the visible confusion and question marks indicate there may be valid uncertainty.
captions.denying-a-remote-hypothetical: Two people in business attire are enthusiastically gesturing toward a rising bar graph, while below them, a man clings desperately to a "DANGER" sign at the edge of a cliff, his face showing fear as the ground crumbles beneath him. The upward trend and cheerful expressions suggest the claim that everything is going well overall, so any rare or extreme problems can be ignored. The important contrast is between the confident, upward-pointing business scene and the immediate peril faced by the man at the edge. We can see that the visible success for the majority does not by itself prove that extreme or unlikely dangers are irrelevant, since the man’s situation is both visible and urgent.
captions.denying-the-antecedent: A scientist holds a paper and examines it with a magnifying glass at a desk, while another man angrily throws a report into a trash bin labeled “TRASH.” The situation suggests that because one report is not peer-reviewed, it must be completely worthless and belongs in the garbage. The important contrast is between the actual status of the report—its lack of peer review being the only visible fact—and the strong conclusion that it has no value at all. We can see that simply not being peer-reviewed does not, by itself, prove a report is worthless, since quality depends on many other factors that are not visible in this scene.
captions.denying-the-correlative: A woman is pointing and looking upset at a smiling man, with a broken heart symbol and an image of a couple kissing above them, while the table shows a torn photograph, motel key, wine glass, and bra. Despite these strong cues suggesting infidelity and relationship problems, the situation is being interpreted as if there is no cheating because the couple is still together. The important contrast is between the visible evidence of betrayal—such as the broken heart, secret kissing, and suspicious objects—and the claim that no real cheating has occurred at all. We can see that the physical clues and emotional reactions alone do not erase the fact that cheating and not cheating are distinct realities, and one cannot simply be denied to remove the other.
captions.division-fallacy: Two well-dressed, smiling people stand in front of a grand university building surrounded by large piles of cash and money bags, while below, a tired-looking older man and a concerned young woman in a lab coat appear in a cluttered laboratory with minimal resources. The image suggests that because the university as a whole appears wealthy, every department or member within it must also have abundant funds. The important contrast is between the visible wealth at the institutional level and the lack of resources seen in the laboratory setting. We can see that the presence of wealth outside does not by itself prove that every part or person within the university enjoys that same financial abundance.
captions.ecological-fallacy: On the left side, we see two smiling adults in front of a school building marked "High Score District," celebrating with a trophy and a rising arrow chart, while on the right a worried boy in a cap holds a failing grade paper and scratches his head under a large question mark. The visual scene suggests the claim that because the district is known for high achievement, any individual student from there—like the boy—must also perform well academically. The important contrast is between the group success and symbols of pride on the left, and the individual student’s visible struggle on the right. We can see that the group statistics and awards do not provide direct evidence about the abilities or performance of any specific person within that group.
captions.empty-refutation: A confident man in a suit holds a folder labeled "CASE CLOSED!" while pushing aside two people, one of whom is gesturing and speaking with a questioning expression. Beside him, a trash bin is filled with papers marked "EVIDENCE," and a board displays charts, documents, a magnifying glass, and an image of a UFO, suggesting an investigation. The important contrast is between the abundant visible evidence and discussion materials versus the man's smug dismissal and finality. We can see that simply declaring a matter settled, without addressing the content of the evidence, does not actually prove that any error, fraud, or flaw has been shown.
captions.epistemic-ontological-conflation: The image shows two people kneeling peacefully in prayer beside lit candles and a steaming bowl, while a person in robes gestures and a thought bubble displays a happy face and a heart; on the other side, a man with binoculars looks confused as he tries to spot a glowing spirit figure. The main claim being inferred from these elements is that the positive emotions and calmness during the ritual are evidence for the real existence of an unseen, supernatural being or force. The important contrast is between the visible, content expressions and ritual objects and the inferred reality of the glowing spirit that cannot be directly seen. We can see people expressing positive feelings while participating in the ritual, but that on its own does not prove the existence of any invisible being or power beyond their experience.
captions.equivocation: The main visible elements are a robot with a brain symbol reading a book, a student raising his hand with a book, and two adults discussing the scene beneath thought bubbles. The impression created is that both the robot and the student are "learning" in the same way, leading to the further claim that the robot understands information just like the human. The important contrast is between the surface actions—reading and recalling facts—which are visible, and the unspoken assumption that these actions mean the robot has human-like comprehension. We can see that the robot’s actions only mimic visible learning behaviors, and this alone does not prove the robot possesses understanding in the human sense.
captions.equivocation-fallacy: The image shows a cheerful robot on a screen saying “I understand,” a smiling man pointing at it, a more menacing robot in a suit pointing forcefully, and a frightened man clutching his head, with a split between the two scenes. The situation implies that because the robot uses the word “understand,” it possesses the same deep, conscious understanding as a human brain, as suggested by the brain symbol in the thought bubble. The important contrast is between the robot’s simple statement with a friendly face and the serious accusation that it has genuine human-level understanding or intelligence. We can see only a robotic face, symbolic speech bubble, and people’s reactions, which do not prove that the robot has the conscious, human-like understanding being claimed.
captions.etymological-fallacy: On the left, an older man stands on a stone block labeled “original meaning,” holding a large book and pointing sternly with a stick, while on the right, a woman points accusingly at him as she and a worried man stand amid dramatic flames. The scene creates the impression of a conflict over word usage, where the man with the book insists on one fixed meaning, suggesting that any modern or emphatic use is wholly incorrect. The important contrast is between the dictionary-focused man standing by a carved definition and the lively pair using the word in an exaggerated, figurative context. We can see strong visual cues of authority and debate, but these alone do not prove that the historical meaning must control how everyone speaks today.
captions.exclusive-premises: At the top, a judge stands between a journalist with a notepad and an activist holding a protest sign, while below them two shadowy figures—one in a fedora, one in a beret—shake hands beneath a large question mark. The visible barriers labeled for each group suggest exclusion, and the handshake between the shaded figures implies a definite connection or separation between the journalist and activist based on their group memberships. The important contrast is between the clear separations shown on the judge’s platform and the inferred handshake—an unseen conclusion based only on exclusionary signs and not on any visible overlap or connection. We can see barriers and the judge’s stern expression, but nothing in this scene actually demonstrates a meaningful link or non-link between the two groups being discussed.
captions.existential-fallacy: The image shows a man with a clipboard pointing toward the forest, a woman excitedly gesturing, and a magnifying glass focusing on an empty pedestal labeled for unicorns, with a thought bubble above them depicting two unicorns hiding behind trees. From these elements, the scene infers that unicorns actually exist in the forest and are just out of sight. The important contrast is between the visible clues—people, trees, and an empty pedestal—and the inferred existence of real unicorns, which are only shown in the thought bubble. We can see that nothing in the visible scene itself directly confirms that there are any unicorns present; the unicorns are imagined, not observed.
captions.fallacy-of-many-questions: A reporter wearing a "PRESS" hat aggressively points at a nervous man seated at a desk with a typewriter, while speech bubbles float above reading accusatory questions, and a poster behind them shows two shadowy figures shaking hands labeled as "NEWSROOM" and "CAMPAIGN." The pointed finger, suspicious facial expressions, and background poster all suggest that there has been a secretive or dishonest collaboration—specifically, collusion or secret meetings—between the newsroom and a campaign. The important contrast is between the visible confrontation and symbols (the question-asking, anxious gestures, and the suggestive poster) and the serious claim being inferred: that guilt and conspiracy are already established facts. We can see an accusation and implication, but nothing in the image actually proves the existence of secret meetings or collusion—it assumes what still needs to be demonstrated.
captions.fallacy-of-necessity: A man sits with his head in his hand, surrounded by crumpled papers labeled "JOBS," while two people point at him and a clock and calendar emphasize the present time; in contrast, on the other side, the same man is now dressed in a suit, waving as he walks confidently toward an office building under a bright sun. The visible scene suggests not only that the man is jobless right now, but tries to infer from that situation that being unemployed is an unchangeable fact about his future. The important contrast is between the current, observable state of unemployment and the inferred claim that this status must always remain true for him. We can see that the man's present predicament does not guarantee his continued unemployment, since nothing in the image’s visible details proves that his situation is permanent or impossible to change.
captions.false-analogy: On one side, a man helps a child with homework using books, while on the other side, a smiling robot assists another child, both scenes showing happy expressions and writing. The image leads to the claim that a robot tutor is just as effective or valuable as a human tutor, indicated by the thought bubble with a graduate and the matched poses. The important contrast is between the visible similarity of two tutors guiding children at a desk, and the inferred belief that the robot can fully replace the human in educational outcomes. We can see the props and gestures are alike, but nothing here proves the robot possesses the same understanding, skills, or empathy that a human tutor offers.
captions.false-attribution: The main visible elements are a smiling elderly man with a medal, a torn photograph of him, a shadowy figure at a typewriter, and a man holding up the photo in front of a doubtful woman. The situation suggests that a respected expert has praised a cure, but this claim is actually being constructed or manipulated by an unknown person. The important contrast is between the visible display of authority and acclaim (the medal and photo) and the hidden, questionable source who is really generating or altering the endorsement. We can see that the mere appearance of expert approval, especially when it is patched together or comes from an anonymous figure, does not prove the expert ever made the claim.
captions.false-balance: Two people, one in a lab coat with a large thermometer and a smoky, melting globe, and the other in a suit holding a protest sign, are shown seated on opposite sides of a balanced scale in a television studio, watched by an audience and filmed by a camera. From this setup, the image suggests that both individuals’ positions on climate change are equally valid or supported. The important contrast is between the visible balance of the scale and stage-like setting, and the reality that the evidence behind each viewpoint is not actually equal. We can see that simply presenting two opposing figures with similar prominence and props on a set does not demonstrate that their claims have equal credibility or evidence behind them.
captions.false-compromise: The image shows three men standing behind large ballot boxes placed on a balance scale: one man on the left is smiling and waving next to a "secure" box, another in the center smiles while holding a "kind of stolen" box, and the third on the right looks angry while pointing at a "stolen" box. From these elements, it is inferred that the truth about the situation must fall in the middle—suggesting the election was partially stolen, simply because there are opposing claims. The important contrast is between the visible presence of three distinct opinions and props on a scale, and the inferred idea that compromise between positions is automatically more accurate. We can see only contrasting characters, facial expressions, and boxes; this setup does not by itself prove any claim about the election’s security or fraud.
captions.false-dilemma: The image shows a politician at a podium, dark scenes of fire, surveillance, and urban danger on one side, and calm park scenes with relaxed people on the other, while a worried couple stands between them. The further claim being inferred is that only two futures are available: pass the bill and get safety, or reject it and get chaos. The important contrast is between the two dramatic options being displayed and the many other policies, tradeoffs, and outcomes left off the stage. We can see a forced choice between fear and peace, but that does not by itself prove that these are the only real possibilities.
captions.false-equivalence: A set of balanced scales holds two men, one looking worried and holding a newspaper marked with a typo under a magnifying glass, the other smiling and presenting a stack of papers labeled with words like "lies" and "fake quotes." By showing both sides equally weighed, the scene pushes the claim that a simple typographical error is just as significant or dishonest as deliberate fabrication and deception. The important contrast is between the visible minor mistake on one side and the collection of serious falsifications on the other, which are not actually alike in impact or intent. We can see that the mere presence of two types of errors on a balanced scale does not prove they are truly equal in seriousness or meaning.
captions.false-surrender: One man angrily points while holding a photo of a black swan and standing next to a chart, while the other man smiles, waves one hand, and raises a white flag, both standing at a table with a scale displaying question marks and a hidden cannon and bomb below. The visible scene suggests the calm man is surrendering or calling for a truce, but the further claim being inferred is that this gesture means both sides are equally valid or that the evidence is inconclusive. The important contrast is between the visible gesture of surrender and balance, and the inferred idea that the debate is now fair or at a draw. We can see the evidence and weapons hidden under the table, so the visual cues do not actually prove that both sides stand on equal ground or that the argument is truly resolved.
captions.faulty-generalization: The image shows two confused robots holding papers with errors while, below them, an angry man points at a smoking broken computer. The further claim being inferred is that because these few examples failed, AI as a whole is useless. The important contrast is between the small number of visible mistakes and the sweeping judgment about every possible case. We can see a few bad outputs and one damaged machine, but that does not by itself prove that all AI systems fail in every context.
captions.for-the-sake-of-argument-denial: The image shows two men in suits, one pointing to a chart with a rising arrow and a money bag, and the other standing defiantly next to a pile of cash labeled “HIGH COSTS.” The man on the right appears to dismiss the other’s case with arms crossed and a skeptical expression, while his thought bubble shows a crossed-out target and a sack of money spilling coins, implying disbelief that the proposed plan will achieve its goals. The important contrast is between the visible situation—one person addressing the costs of an idea using visual evidence, and the other rejecting even the cost argument based on his disbelief in the plan’s success. We can see that simply doubting the plan’s chances does not address whether the cost argument itself would be valid if the plan did succeed.
captions.four-terms-fallacy: Two people are shown arguing at podiums, with a large question mark above them, while below, a man happily holds a large sandwich, and an empty chair marked "Nothing" sits to the side. From these images, the scene infers that because "nothing is better than debate" and "a sandwich is better than nothing," the sandwich must be better than debate itself. The important contrast is between the visible argument about values at the podium and the playful use of an empty chair and sandwich to connect two unrelated meanings of "nothing." We can see that the literal empty chair and the food do not logically link the value of open debate to the tastiness of a sandwich.
captions.gambler-s-fallacy: A man points excitedly at a chart showing a sequence of coins all landing heads, while a concerned woman looks on and a blindfolded figure flips another coin and holds a balanced scale. The visible sequence of heads and the man's confident gesture suggest he believes the next flip must be tails, as if fate or inevitability demands a reversal. The important contrast is between the simple facts of the previous coin flips, which are laid out clearly, and the man's leap to an unseen force making tails “due” next. We can see a fair coin and random flips, but nothing in the visible setup guarantees that the odds have changed for the future outcome.
captions.genetic-fallacy: The image shows two sharply divided groups: on the left, two people in business attire with angry, skeptical expressions point accusingly toward a smartphone displaying a recognizable app logo; on the right, two cheerful people present a chart with a glowing lightbulb and upward trend line. From these elements, the scene infers that an idea or proposal must be untrustworthy or foolish simply because it originated from the app shown on the phone. The important contrast is between the visible skepticism and dismissal based purely on where the idea came from versus the apparent success and positive results shown in the presentation. We can see that knowing the source of the idea by itself does not prove anything about the merit or effectiveness of what is being proposed.
captions.hasty-generalization: A man in a suit points at a clipboard with a small survey of faces, while a magnifying glass zooms in on two students at a desk admitting to cheating, and a second pair of students sits in the background. The entire scene suggests that because two students confessed to cheating, it is reasonable to conclude that AI is completely ruining education for everyone. The important contrast is between the tiny, specific group actually shown and the sweeping claim about the entire educational system that is being inferred from them. We can see only a couple of students confessing, but that alone does not prove that all or most students are cheating or that AI is universally harmful to education.
captions.historian-s-fallacy: The image shows a cheerful man in a suit holding a document marked "2007" beside rising charts, while on the other side, two worried people use a telescope to spot a dramatic stock market crash, with a large red arrow crashing into buildings and people fleeing. The visible scene suggests that people in 2007 should have clearly seen the financial collapse coming, as if the warning signs were obvious at the time. The important contrast is between the confident, optimistic behavior and upward trends visible in the 2007 section and the hindsight view of disaster shown on the right side. We can see that the people in 2007 only had access to rising charts and optimism, not the later evidence of crisis, so the scene by itself does not prove they could foresee what would happen.
captions.homunculus-fallacy: A cutaway of a head shows a film projector beaming an image into the brain, where a small person sits on a chair and studies a picture, while outside the head, a puzzled scientist scratches his head with a clipboard in hand. This scene suggests the idea that perception happens because there is a tiny inner observer inside our heads watching images. The important contrast is between the actual physical parts we can see—a brain, a mechanical projector, and images—and the inferred presence of a mind-like observer inside the brain, which is not visible or explained. We can see that the image only shows physical objects and does not provide evidence for a separate “inner viewer,” so it does not solve how perception really works.
captions.human-standard-fallacy: The image shows two smiling people eagerly pinning a large sign labeled "FALSE" over a picture of the globe, while another distressed person gestures and protests below. From these elements, the further claim being inferred is that the official action of labeling something as "false" or "misinformation" instantly makes it actually false in reality. The important contrast is between the visible act of posting a label and the much larger, unseen truth or falsity of the underlying claim about the world. We can see people putting up signs and reacting, but this alone does not prove that the content in question became false simply because someone applied a label to it.
captions.if-by-whiskey: The image is split into two sides, each showing a man at a podium labeled "AI Regulation," with one side featuring a robot and a padlock, and the other a rocket, gears, and a snail. The immediate impression is that the same policy is being linked either to preventing harm from robots or to slowing down technological progress. The important contrast is between the clear, specific objects—robot, padlock, rocket, snail—and the shifting meaning inferred from "AI regulation" depending on which outcome the speaker wants to highlight. We can see the visual elements reflect two opposing implications, but the images themselves do not prove that a single policy must lead only to safety or only to delay.
captions.illicit-major: The image shows a glamorous couple in formalwear waving to cameras at a red-carpet event labeled "Famous People" and "VIP Party," while two teachers holding books stand behind a rope with a sign that says "No Teachers Allowed" near a classroom. From these elements, the further claim being inferred is that no teachers can ever be famous, suggesting a strict separation of fame and teaching. The important contrast is between the visible division of spaces by the rope and signs, and the inferred universal exclusion implied about teachers and fame. We can see only two groups in a staged scene, which does not by itself prove that no teachers are or could be famous.
captions.impotent-logical-space: A woman sits at a table with a crystal ball and tarot cards, gesturing confidently, while two scenes above her show contrasting outcomes: one with people huddling under an umbrella during a storm, and the other with cheerful people celebrating in sunny weather. From these elements, the claim being inferred is that the woman’s powers are proven no matter what happens—if disaster strikes, she predicted it, and if things go well, she caused the good outcome. The important contrast is between the physical situations—bad weather or good weather—and the claim that the same person deserves credit both for a warning coming true and for a positive outcome. We can see that the image only shows separate outcomes and the woman’s repeating gesture, but this alone cannot establish that she truly caused or predicted anything, since neither result would ever count as evidence against her claim.
captions.incomplete-comparison: On the left side, a smiling man and woman stand in front of a sign advertising rent for $800, with small houses, a smoking car, and factories in the background. On the right side, a stressed man on the phone and a woman holding a drink stand near a sign showing rent for $3,000, with skyscrapers, an airplane, a fancy meal, and drinks behind them. The important contrast is between the visible cost of rent and the broader lifestyle cues such as job salaries, travel, and local environment that are hinted at but not clearly compared. We can see that the lower rent alone does not prove a place is overall more affordable or desirable, because other important factors are not fully shown or measured in the image.
captions.inconsistent-comparison: A man in a suit holds a glowing laptop triumphantly above his head, while on either side, two people point to different laptops labeled with price tags and a scale with a feather, suggesting cost and speed. From these elements, the claim is being inferred that the central laptop must be the overall best choice because it is cheaper than one rival and faster than another, suggesting superiority in every category. The important contrast is between the visible separate comparisons—one with price, one with speed—and the inferred conclusion that one laptop dominates all others in every important way. We can see that each comparison uses a different opponent, so the visible examples alone do not justify the claim that this laptop is plainly the best overall.
captions.intentional-fallacy: A man holding a paper labeled "SATIRE!" stands anxiously beside a trash can, while two others at a desk intently examine an essay using a large magnifying glass and point sharply. The impression created is that the claim of satire is ignored, with all focus on the essay's contents and the group's own strict interpretation. The important contrast is between the visible demonstration of the author's intention—his display of the "SATIRE!" sheet—and the inference by the seated group that their interpretation alone matters for understanding the essay. We can see that the author is plainly presenting his intent, but this visible act does not by itself prove that the group's chosen interpretation is correct or justified.
captions.is-ought-problem: The image features a split scene: the top shows workers at desks with headsets, watched by a camera and overseen by a smiling man pointing down, while the bottom shows two people with crossed arms looking unhappy, beside a large thumbs-up and a sign urging acceptance. The implication is that because workplace surveillance is happening and increasing, people are supposed to agree that such monitoring is the correct or inevitable way things should be. The important contrast is between the visible reality of surveillance equipment and the workers' reactions, and the inferred idea that acceptance is morally required just because something is common. We can see the monitoring and the pressure to comply, but these images alone offer no justification for why being watched ought to be accepted as good or right.
captions.judgmental-language: A man at a podium is aggressively pointing and shouting, while a crowd cheers and another man stands off to the side looking alarmed, his shadow labeled with an insult. The scene suggests that simply disagreeing with the speaker makes the second man a coward, as shown by the exaggerated shadow and the way the crowd responds approvingly. The important contrast is between the actual disagreement visibly taking place and the harsh label of cowardice that is imposed on the second man. We can see that the use of an insult, combined with the crowd’s reaction and discarded piles labeled as reasons, does not provide any real evidence that the man’s disagreement is cowardly.
captions.linearity-fallacy: A smiling gardener is shown pouring water from two watering cans onto a drooping plant, while a flourishing flower in a separate pot sits nearby next to a large measuring stick and a sharply rising arrow. The scene suggests that by using twice as much water, the plant should grow twice as fast or large, implying a guaranteed direct cause-and-effect relationship between effort and outcome. The important contrast is between the visible act of doubling the watering and the inferred belief in automatic double growth. We can see from the wilted, overwatered plant and the healthy, steadily-grown flower that simply increasing input does not always produce the assumed proportional result.
captions.luddite-fallacy: The image shows worried jobless workers on one side and, on the other, a cheerful robot and mechanical arm processing paperwork with speed and ease. The further claim being inferred is that because machines can do this task, people will be left with no work and no useful role at all. The important contrast is between the visible automation of one kind of job and the much larger conclusion that human usefulness must disappear. We can see technology replacing a specific task, but that does not by itself prove that all employment, adaptation, or new forms of work are gone.
captions.masked-man-fallacy: A stern man points accusingly toward a mysterious masked figure holding a paper, while in another part of the image, a similar-looking man writes at a desk beneath a framed portrait. From these clues, someone is inferring that the masked, secretive figure is definitely not the same person as the man in the portrait, simply because the masked figure’s identity is hidden. The important contrast is between the visible cues of disguise and secrecy, and the inferred certainty that two figures must be different people. We can see faces, clothing, and actions, but these visible signs alone do not prove whether the man known publicly is or is not the author in disguise.
captions.misleading-vividness: The image shows a dramatic split scene: in the lower half, a masked attacker with a knife threatens a frightened woman and a cowering man near a subway, while in the upper half, two shocked people react with wide eyes and urgent gestures in a calmer outdoor setting. From these elements, the further claim being inferred is that subway attacks like the one depicted are common or representative of city life, suggesting a general atmosphere of chaos or danger. The important contrast is between the single vivid incident of violence and the sweeping generalization that similar danger is everywhere or increasing. We can see that a single intense event, even if alarming, does not by itself show how frequent or widespread such incidents truly are.
captions.motte-and-bailey-fallacy: The image shows a man in medieval clothing standing confidently on a stone platform, pointing and addressing a group of shadowy figures, while a fortified tower with a worried man inside is connected to him by bold arrows. The situation creates the impression that he alternates between making a bold accusation and retreating to the safety of the fortified tower, suggesting he is inferring extra protection or justification from the stronghold. The important contrast is between the visible confident claims and retreat on the open platform versus the more cautious, defensive posture inside the tower. We can see that the visual transition between the platform and the tower does not itself prove that the strong claim and the weaker, safer claim are actually the same or equally justified.
captions.moving-the-goalpost: A smiling woman stands at a finish line holding a certificate, while confetti falls and two men below point and argue. To the right, a new, more distant goalpost appears in front of a busy office scene with a robot in a suit, surrounded by paperwork. The important contrast is between the clearly achieved goal in the left scene and the shifting, harder requirement symbolized by the new goalpost on the right. We can see that passing the bar exam is visibly and concretely accomplished, but nothing in this scene by itself proves that running an entire law firm must be the new standard for usefulness.
captions.naturalistic-fallacy: The image shows a smiling farmer and woman holding a jar of milk near flowers, a concerned doctor with a carton, and a cow next to a barn, a milking stool, laboratory vials, and a skull. From these elements, the claim is being inferred that raw, “natural” milk is safer or healthier just because it comes straight from the cow, while anything processed is suspicious or harmful. The important contrast is between the cheerful presentation of the fresh milk and nature, and the implied danger and risk shown by the scientist’s alarm, laboratory glassware, and the skull next to the cow. We can see happy faces, farm scenery, and props, but these images do not by themselves prove that untreated milk is better or safer than pasteurized milk.
captions.negative-proof-fallacy: A voting machine sits open, with one person excitedly pointing inside and another peering in with suspicion, while arrows and wires lead toward a label that hints at secret software. The scene suggests that, because no one has disproven the presence of hidden vote-switching software, it must therefore exist and control the election outcome. The important contrast is between the visible voting machine components and arrows, and the inferred existence of a hidden, manipulative software that determines winners and losers. We can see concerned and suspicious expressions and circuit boards, but nothing here proves that such secret software is actually installed or operating.
captions.nirvana-fallacy: The image shows a stern man in a suit holding a carbon label, a worker with a CO2 bottle, and a radiant angel holding the globe, separated by a wide chasm, with factories and pollution on one side and clean energy like solar panels and wind turbines on the other. From these elements, the image suggests that only a perfect, angelic solution can solve environmental problems, with any practical measure like carbon labeling dismissed as insufficient. The important contrast is between the realistic, imperfect action presented by the suited man and the impossible, flawless paradise represented by the angel. We can see that the factories, chasm, and practical proposals are real and tangible, but the angel and idealized world do not offer practical steps or evidence that incremental solutions are useless.
captions.no-true-scotsman: There is a man in a suit and hat angrily pointing toward two smiling men, one of whom holds a paper labeled "IMMIGRATION BILL," while a sign reading "REAL CONSERVATIVES ONLY!" stands between them. The scene suggests that the man pointing is accusing the others of not being genuine members of his group based on their support for the bill. The important contrast is between the visible disagreement over a political issue and the inferred claim that only certain people count as "real" members, with the definition shifting to exclude those who disagree. We can see the people, the sign, and their expressions, but nothing in the visible scene proves or defines who is truly a member—only that there is a disagreement and an attempt to exclude.
captions.overwhelming-exception: A man stands at a podium holding up a sign for free speech, surrounded by four other people holding signs listing various reasons for exceptions, each with concerned or disapproving faces. The impression created is that free speech is being championed, but at the same time, many objections are being raised, suggesting only limited support under strict conditions. The important contrast is between the highly visible display of support for free speech and the overwhelming number of exceptions that seem to undermine that support. We can see that the visible protest signs and gestures do not by themselves prove that free speech is truly valued in practice when so many major exceptions are attached.
captions.package-deal-fallacy: The image shows two split scenes: on the left, a boy with a serious expression wearing a headset and hoodie is playing video games beneath signs with stark images, while on the right, a smiling girl in a headset also plays, as two adults react with surprise and accusation. From these elements, the assumption is being inferred that gamers must fit a package of traits like being male and antisocial, while the girl's presence is treated as surprising or invalid by the adults. The important contrast is between the visible diversity among gamers and the inflexible expectations suggested by the posters and adults' gestures. We can see that simply playing video games does not guarantee that someone has a particular personality, gender, or social habits, so the visible scene does not prove the rigid package of traits some expect.
captions.pathetic-fallacy: A large, menacing figure with a dollar sign hat, sharp teeth, and a whip looms over scared people and a document labeled “reform plan,” while a man in a suit points toward the figure. The image suggests that the visible chaos and fear are caused by the market itself having human-like anger and intentions. The important contrast is between the dramatic, personified monster towering above and the actual stock chart line and worried people below. We can see fear and distress in people’s expressions, but nothing in this scene proves that the market has thoughts or emotions like a person.
captions.perfect-solution-fallacy: The image shows a smiling builder and woman talking in front of new buildings and construction cranes, while an angry man points at a “HIGH RENT$” sign and imagines a run-down house. The scene suggests that even with new housing being built, the problem of expensive or poor-quality housing will remain unchanged. The important contrast is between the visible construction efforts and hopeful expressions, and the inferred idea that these efforts are pointless because all housing problems will persist. We can see new buildings rising and people engaging constructively, but nothing here shows that building more homes cannot improve rents or living conditions at all.
