captions.perfect-standard: The image shows a worried journalist at a desk with a microphone and papers, while two angry people point and yell at him; above them, there are exaggerated figures of an angel on a pedestal labeled “perfect” and a devil in flames labeled “liar.” This scene suggests that any mistake the journalist makes will force him into one of two extreme categories: perfectly good or utterly evil, as symbolized by the angel and devil watching over the moment. The important contrast is between the real, anxious person who is simply doing their job and the rigid, fantastical categories of moral perfection or total dishonesty imposed from above. We can see that the visible situation—a person making a mistake and others reacting—is not enough to prove anyone deserves to be treated as entirely pure or entirely false.
captions.perverted-analogy: A worried-looking man in a suit holds an insurance policy while sitting at a desk, as a doctor in a white coat, mask, and stethoscope examines a test tube with a magnifying glass beside him. The immediate scene creates an odd clash between a business office, represented by the desk and financial chart with a dollar sign, and a medical investigation. From these elements, the claim being inferred is that comparing public-health measures to insurance is foolish because insurance companies do not employ doctors or scientists. The important contrast is between the visible separation of business and medical roles and the implication that one must mirror the other in every detail for the analogy to be meaningful. We can see that the visible scene only highlights superficial differences and does not actually disprove the underlying comparison between public-health policies and insurance.
captions.piggy-back-assumption: Two men in trench coats are shown, with one sitting on the other's shoulders; the lower man is smiling and holding a paper about a stage door, while the man on top points excitedly and waves a paper labeled with a conspiracy. In the background, a shadowy scene shows two figures shaking hands under the moonlight next to a briefcase full of cash, suggesting the existence of a hidden, sinister deal. The important contrast is between the concrete, specific evidence about a stage door and the sweeping accusation of a vast secret plot. We can see that having a correct detail about the stage door does not by itself prove the entire conspiracy shown in the background.
captions.poisoning-the-well: Two men with scheming expressions are shown whispering together while one pours a dark liquid labeled with a skull into a stone well; nearby, a woman at a podium is speaking and two listeners frown in suspicion. The image suggests that because the men have tainted the scene beforehand, anything the woman says will already be viewed with distrust or dismissed as poisoned by hidden motives. The important contrast is between the visible act of sabotage—pouring "slander" into the well and whispering—and the audience's sudden certainty that the speaker cannot be trusted, even before she presents her ideas. We can see that the onlookers' suspicion does not logically follow from the woman’s actions at the podium but is triggered by the men’s deliberate attempt to bias them in advance.
captions.post-hoc-ergo-propter-hoc: A person sits at a table on Monday holding their head in pain, surrounded by pills and emphasized by red zigzag lines, while on Friday, the same person appears joyful with raised arms and musical notes around their head. The scene suggests that taking the pills directly caused the shift from suffering to happiness and good health, as shown by the large arrows connecting the two situations and an image of a smiling sun. The important contrast is between the actual visible actions—a person taking pills and later feeling better—and the inferred conclusion that the pills themselves must be responsible for the recovery. We can see the time sequence and emotional changes, but nothing in the image proves that the medicine caused the improvement, since no other possible explanations are shown or ruled out.
captions.proof-by-example: A smiling man is seated at a desk giving a thumbs-up to two cheerful robots in business attire, while another man points excitedly toward a scene of well-dressed people, some appearing confident and one looking anxious. From these visuals, the viewer is led to infer that because this single man is happy with his robot coworkers, robots must be capable of replacing all professionals in similar jobs. The important contrast is between the concrete example of one man’s satisfaction with helpful robots and the much larger claim that robots are universally suitable replacements for all office workers. We can see only one positive result in a specific case, which does not by itself provide enough evidence to justify a sweeping conclusion about all jobs or all robots.
captions.proof-by-verbosity: A man in a suit stands above a huge pile of documents, gesturing confidently and holding a long sheet, while another overwhelmed man sits at a desk buried under papers with a confused expression and question marks above his head. This scene suggests that the sheer volume of paperwork and arguments is supposed to prove the standing man's point or give the impression that his claims are unchallengeable because they are too extensive to address. The important contrast is between the visible mass of documents and confident gestures, and the inferred conclusion that quantity of arguments alone guarantees correctness. We can see that a flood of paperwork can confuse or exhaust someone, but by itself it does not demonstrate that any individual claim is true.
captions.prosecutor-s-fallacy: A confident prosecutor holds up a large portrait labeled “99.9% match” toward a worried, handcuffed man, while a judge and police officer look on in a courtroom. From these elements, the further claim is being inferred that, because the DNA or facial recognition match is so accurate, the man on trial must certainly be guilty, with no real chance of innocence. The important contrast is between the visible evidence of a strong DNA match and the much bigger, unseen leap to the man’s actual guilt. We can see the props, symbols, and anxious expression, but the scene alone does not prove that the match result directly means this specific person is guilty, since it ignores the real chance of a coincidental match among a large population.
captions.psychologist-s-fallacy: A worried man is shown clasping his hands in front of his face, with a thought bubble containing a devil, a dancing woman, and a cocktail, while facing two calm people standing outside a church. The image suggests that the man assumes the other two people have the same temptations and inner struggles he does, perhaps believing that their need for religion mirrors his own. The important contrast is between the visible anxiety and fantasies in the man’s mind and the neutral, composed appearance of the couple near the church. We can see only the man’s imagined scene and the outward behavior of the other two, which does not provide evidence about their private motives or thoughts.
captions.red-herring: A man stands at a podium with buildings behind him, while another man points and gestures in front of a barbed-wire fence and guard tower; between them, a large red fish swoops across, catching the attention of the audience below. The scene suggests that when asked about housing costs, the speaker diverts to a dramatic but unrelated issue, implied by the fish and the change in background. The important contrast is between the visible question about housing, represented by the podium and cityscape, and the inferred shift to a different, emotionally charged topic, represented by the fence and fish. We can see that the mere presence of the fish and the dramatic gesture do not address or resolve the original question about housing, but simply change the subject.
captions.redeeming-illogic-with-evidence: A man in a lab coat enthusiastically points to a chart on an easel that displays a shape labeled "Square Triangle," while another man in a suit looks confused and holds his head near a table with a microscope and magnifying glass. The image implies that careful data analysis or laboratory investigation could prove the existence of a "square triangle," which is a contradiction in terms. The important contrast is between the visible scientific props and charts, which suggest investigation and evidence, and the logically impossible concept being promoted as if evidence could make it real. We can see that the presence of data, graphs, and lab equipment cannot validate an idea that is self-contradictory before any evidence is considered.
captions.regression-fallacy: The main visible elements are an adult angrily pointing and scolding a sad student holding a paper marked “F,” a graph showing a rising arrow from “F” to “B,” and finally the same student smiling and giving a thumbs up while showing a “B” paper, with the adult now smugly satisfied. From these scenes, it is inferred that the adult’s angry lecture directly caused the student’s improved grade and that this intervention has special power to change performance. The important contrast is between the visible sequence of anger, a test result, a graph, and a happier outcome, and the unseen assumption that the lecture alone was the decisive force behind the improvement. We can see disappointment, a dramatic gesture, and better grades, but there is no direct proof that the verbal scolding actually caused the student’s score to return to normal.
captions.reification: The image shows a large, menacing figure in a suit with a monster-like face breathing fire onto a plunging stock arrow, while two frightened people sit at a desk with a broken piggy bank and scattered coins. From these elements, it is inferred that an abstract force, depicted as a physical monster, is personally attacking people's finances and causing their distress. The important contrast is between the visible, concrete depiction of a monster causing harm and the fact that the actual subject—such as the market or economic trends—is not a real creature with desires or intentions. We can see the visual cues of fear, destruction, and the monster's dramatic gesture, but these only show people's reactions and losses, not real evidence that an invisible beast is behind the situation.
captions.retrospective-determinism: The image shows, in the top half, two people confidently pointing at a destroyed building with smoke and a “FAILED” sign, while in the bottom half, two worried people sit among charts, dice, and question marks. The scene is used to infer that the building’s failure was always clear, as if collapse had been obvious from the start. The important contrast is between the certainty and smugness after disaster strikes, and the uncertainty, confusion, and randomness present beforehand. We can see from the visible doubt, sweat, and dice in the lower scene that the outcome was not predictable at the earlier stage, so the later certainty is not justified by the evidence shown.
captions.semantic-pixelization: Two people are arguing in front of a colored scale that fades gradually from green "safe" to red "unsafe," with a rocket and an explosion shown at the bottom. One person gestures calmly, while the other points aggressively, forcing a choice between two extreme signs that say “100% safe” and “total disaster.” The important contrast is between the visible gradual safety scale and the rigid, all-or-nothing choices being presented by the second person. We can see that the existence of a spectrum and the measured body language do not by themselves prove that safety and danger must be absolute opposites.
captions.sentimental-fallacy: The main visible elements are two worried doctors holding a clipboard marked with a large red X, medical bottles, and a trash can filled with discarded papers, contrasted with hopeful people imagining a man happily standing from his wheelchair, surrounded by hearts and smiling family members. From these elements, the further claim being inferred is that a joyful, miraculous recovery is possible just because it would be emotionally uplifting and desirable. The important contrast is between the clear evidence of failed medical treatment shown by the doctors and the wishful vision of a perfect outcome imagined by the onlookers. We can see that while the scene shows disappointment and failed attempts on one side, this alone does not prove that the happy recovery imagined by others is actually possible.
captions.sharpshooter-fallacy: A man in a suit is proudly gesturing toward a target covered in tightly grouped bullet holes, with several other targets showing scattered patterns nearby, while two other figures observe with a clipboard and binoculars, and a map labeled with different crime areas lies on the ground. From these elements, the image implies that the man demonstrated real skill or caused a dramatic reduction in crime in a specific area by achieving such a perfect result. The important contrast is between the visibly cherry-picked target with clustered hits or the circled “low crime” area and the other ignored targets and marked neighborhoods scattered around it. We can see that selecting only the favorable target or area after seeing all the results does not, by itself, prove any claim about ability or causal success.
captions.single-cause-fallacy: The image shows a smiling man in a suit standing on a pedestal, proudly holding a blazing arrow labeled "INFLATION," while worried people look up at him and industrial scenes like oil barrels, factories, and a cargo ship fill the background. From these elements, the image infers that only the man’s specific policy caused inflation, ignoring other factors like oil prices, supply issues, and money printing suggested by the industrial props. The important contrast is between the complex, chaotic background with multiple possible causes and the single, triumphant figure pointing to one explanation. We can see that the existence of many visual sources of trouble in the scene means the simple answer offered by the man alone does not account for all that might have led to inflation.
captions.slippery-slope: There is a group of people tumbling rapidly down a steep slope from a desk with a computer, ending in a chaotic scene at a university table where a robotic-looking graduate is automatically stamping papers. The image suggests that allowing students to use AI for brainstorming will inevitably lead to a future where learning collapses and universities are run entirely by unthinking machines. The important contrast is between the single visible action at the top—a person pointing to a computer—and the exaggerated disaster at the bottom, where normal academic processes are replaced by mindless automation. We can see only a dramatic sequence of falling people and a robotic figure, which does not by itself prove that one small choice must cause everything else to collapse in the way shown.
captions.special-pleading: A man in a spotlight proudly displays a phone with a heart symbol, while two concerned people point toward a sign with a lock and a large bag labeled for holding important data. The scene suggests that the man is claiming his app deserves special treatment and exemption from normal privacy standards without showing any real reason why. The important contrast is between the clear demand for privacy shown by the lock symbol and the bag of sensitive information, and the man's confident attitude implying his app alone should be excused. We can see enthusiastic gestures and props, but nothing visible in the image actually justifies why this app would be exempt from the expectations applied to everyone else.
captions.spotlight-fallacy: A large spotlight highlights two masked figures holding a club and a flaming bottle amid smoke, while a crowd of protesters with signs stands in the dim background and a person in the foreground observes the scene on a smartphone. From these elements, the image suggests that the most visible, violent individuals are being taken as typical of the entire protest group. The important contrast is between the dramatic, illuminated actions of the few at the front and the less visible, nonviolent crowd in the background. We can see that only a small part of the protest is caught in the spotlight, so this view alone does not prove that the whole crowd shares the same violent behavior.
captions.square-logic: A worried man sits trapped within a tangled, geometric structure of twisting arrows, while two figures point at him—one holding a "Denied" sign and the other grinning. The arrows loop endlessly, suggesting an argument turning in on itself, while two open file drawers labeled "False" and "Truth" imply that the man’s situation is being used to judge what is real or fake. The important contrast is between the confused, circular scene and the implied claim that the denial itself reveals some hidden truth or falsehood. We can see only the complicated argument and emotional reactions, not any actual evidence that the denial settles what is true or false.
captions.straw-man-argument: The main visible elements are two calm speakers at a podium, a shouting man pointing dramatically, a burning straw figure with a sign, and two shocked onlookers. From these elements, the scene suggests that the angry man is accusing the speakers of wanting to impose an extreme and unpopular action, as represented by the exaggerated claim on the burning straw figure. The important contrast is between the poised discussion at the podium and the theatrical destruction of a fake opponent representing a distorted version of their position. We can see that the presence of a burning straw figure and dramatic gestures do not actually prove the speakers support the extreme view being attacked.
captions.style-over-substance-fallacy: The image shows a confident woman joyfully speaking at a podium under spotlights, surrounded by enthusiastic cheering crowds, while a worried man with glasses holds a sheet labeled with question marks and facts. The scene suggests that the woman’s charisma and dramatic gestures are being taken as proof that her argument is correct, even above the hesitant man’s factual approach. The important contrast is between the visible excitement, applause, and stage presence of the speaker, and the unseen claim that these qualities determine the truth or value of her message. We can see that the dramatic crowd reaction and confident posture do not actually demonstrate the quality or validity of what is being argued.
captions.suppressed-correlative: The image shows a smoking man on a chair, a smiling doctor, and two athletic men standing on a winner’s podium labeled “Fitter” and “Fittest,” with arrows pointing from “Fit” to “Fitter” to “Fittest.” The impression is that only those at the very top of physical condition can truly be considered “fit,” while everyone else is put into relative categories below them. The important contrast is between the visible range of health among the figures (from unhealthy, to fit, to fittest) and the inferred claim that only the absolute healthiest person deserves the label “fit.” We can see several gradations of health, but nothing in the scene by itself shows that the existence of healthier people actually erases the meaningfulness of calling others “fit.”
captions.survivorship-bias: At the top, three cheerful people in business suits stand on steps with a rising arrow and a college building behind them, appearing successful and triumphant, while a smiling figure points at them. Below, several anxious or distressed graduates in caps and gowns sit in a pit surrounded by scattered papers, one holding a failing grade. The important contrast is between the visible successes who skipped college and are highlighted above, and the overlooked failures or struggling graduates below. We can see only a few visible winners and many unnoticed strugglers, so this scene does not by itself prove that skipping college usually leads to wealth or that college is unnecessary for success.
captions.teleological-fallacy: The image shows an evolutionary sequence with ape-like figures progressing toward a modern human, who sits smiling on a bullseye spotlight, while a person below holds a brain diagram and points upward; nearby, a confused ape scratches its head with a question mark. The scene suggests the claim that human intelligence and form were the intended purpose or final destination of evolution, as if guided toward this endpoint. The important contrast is between the clear visuals of gradual physical changes and confident gestures, and the inferred idea of a predetermined goal or hidden intention guiding the entire evolutionary process. We can see stages of development and signs of planning in the human's actions, but nothing in the visible sequence proves that the process itself was aimed specifically at producing modern humans or intelligence.
captions.thought-terminating-clich: The image shows a confident man in a suit standing on a locked pedestal spotlighted at the center, with two people on the side holding paperwork and a magnifying glass while pointing toward him. From these elements, the impression is created that the man’s dismissive gesture and posture have caused the investigative efforts to be halted, implying further questioning or scrutiny is impossible or unnecessary. The important contrast is between the visible investigators’ active search for answers and the man’s relaxed insistence that nothing more can or should be done. We can see that the mere presence of the man’s shrug and the locked pedestal do not prove the investigation is truly finished or that there are no questions left to address.
captions.top-down-condemnation: A man in a suit angrily points while imagining a shady-looking driver taking money, and in the foreground, a surprised taxi driver stands in front of his car with other worried drivers behind him. The scene suggests that, because one driver committed a scam, all taxi or rideshare drivers must be criminals, as illustrated by the shadowy crooks holding a money bag near the cab. The important contrast is between the single criminal act imagined in the thought bubble and the group of ordinary drivers being judged on that basis. We can see visible props like the taxi, uniforms, and exaggerated gestures, but nothing here alone proves that every driver in the group is guilty of wrongdoing.
captions.top-down-faulty-generalization: A man in a suit points angrily at a runner while holding a bowl full of sugar cubes beside a plate with a donut and a drink, creating a scene of conflict over dietary choices. From these elements, the claim is inferred that if sugar can be used by runners for energy during a race, then any general claim that sugar is unhealthy must be false in all circumstances. The important contrast is between the visible special context of sports performance and the broader claim about sugar’s overall health effects in everyday situations. We can see that the runner taking energy gel during a race does not by itself disprove the idea that sugar may be unhealthy for the general population.
captions.top-down-justification: At the top, a smiling repairman gives a thumbs-up in front of a house, highlighted by sparkling light, while next to him a happy man in a suit points upward. Below, three stern men—one with a cigar, one with a sly grin, and another holding an eviction notice—stand together with crossed arms, creating a feeling of tension and mistrust. From the friendly repairman, the claim is inferred that all landlords must be caring and responsible, despite the presence of these much harsher figures. The important contrast is between the visible kindness of one individual and the mixed or negative attitudes of the group below. We can see that showing one friendly landlord does not actually demonstrate that the whole group shares those positive traits.
captions.track-record-reset: On the left side, there is a bulletin board filled with papers marked "FALSE!" and skeptical people pointing at them, while a broom is sweeping these papers away; on the right side, a cheerful robed figure stands before a glowing mountain, raising their arms beside praising onlookers and a sign promising a miracle. The scene suggests that despite a long history of failed predictions being visibly removed or ignored, people are now inferring that a powerful miracle is about to happen simply based on the new claim. The important contrast is between the obvious evidence of prior failures and the sudden leap to renewed belief in an extraordinary event. We can see that the happy expressions, dramatic gestures, and glowing background do not erase the repeated, documented track record of past mistakes, so the claim lacks support from the visible facts alone.
captions.tu-quoque: The image shows two angry men confronting each other, one holding a paper labeled "FAKE QUOTE" and the other pointing an accusing finger, as well as scenes of a politician at a podium and a person at a computer with words about lies and fake news. The further claim being inferred from these elements is that because one side has committed wrongdoing or dishonesty, any charges of similar behavior from the other side must be dismissed or are equally invalid. The important contrast is between the visible accusations and emotional gestures (pointing, shouting, holding papers) and the inferred idea that hypocrisy alone cancels out the criticism or proves innocence. We can see people accusing each other and pointing to others’ faults, but this alone does not logically demonstrate that the original charge is false or unworthy of consideration.
captions.two-wrongs-make-a-right: Two groups of people are shown, each passing a film reel labeled "FAKE" to one another with sly smiles, then angrily broadcasting the reels on old-fashioned televisions, while children watch in surprise. The image suggests the claim that creating deceptive media is acceptable as retaliation because the opposing side has done the same thing. The important contrast is between the direct acts of spreading fake information visible in the picture and the inferred justification that one wrong action balances out or excuses another. We can see both groups committing the same offense, but nothing in the scene itself proves that this repetition turns either act into a right or makes it justified.
captions.undistributed-middle: The image features two people in trench coats and tinfoil hats, gesturing and wearing dark glasses and binoculars, next to a man in business clothes standing before official-looking buildings labeled as a courthouse and a bank. The situation suggests that both the conspiracy-minded pair and the businessman share a suspicious attitude toward institutions, and from this, the claim is inferred that the businessman is himself a conspiracy theorist. The important contrast is between the visible signs of conspiracy thinking (like tinfoil hats, secretive gestures, and elaborate background diagrams) and the simple distrustful stance of the businessman. We can see that simply distrusting institutions does not by itself justify concluding that someone embraces conspiracy theories, since visible behaviors and underlying beliefs differ.
captions.vague-insulators: A smiling man in a suit holds up a jar of capsules while gesturing enthusiastically, a meditating woman floats above surrounded by glowing clouds, stars, and a crescent moon, and another man examines a jar labeled "Mystic Pills" using a magnifying glass next to a microscope and checklist. The image suggests that these pills offer hidden or mystical benefits by invoking ideas of inner energies or spiritual harmony, which are shown as glowing clouds and celestial symbols. The important contrast is between the fanciful, magical atmosphere and symbols surrounding the pills and the attempt by the serious investigator to test or verify them with scientific tools. We can see clouds, light, and symbols around the woman and pills, but these effects do not provide concrete evidence that the pills have any real, testable mystical power.
captions.wishful-thinking: The image shows a sharply dressed man smiling confidently while holding cash and a drink, with two anxious onlookers in front of a steeply falling stock chart marked "CRASH." Despite the visible market crash, the man imagines a rocket with a dollar sign soaring upward, implying his belief that fortunes are bound to improve soon. The important contrast is between the real scene of panic and financial downturn, and the man’s hopeful vision of sudden recovery and profit. We can see worried expressions, falling stock values, and crisis, but nothing in this scene actually supports the certainty of a rapid financial rebound.
captions.witness-chain: A man in a suit stands with one hand on his chest and points upward excitedly, with glowing light above and a group of shadowy figures with question marks in the background; in front, empty roped-off seats display a sign reading "SORRY NOT AVAILABLE." The situation suggests he claims to have witnessed a miraculous event and insists many others, represented by the indistinct figures, can back him up, even though these supposed witnesses remain unavailable and vague. The important contrast is between the man’s visible enthusiasm and certainty, along with the empty seats and mysterious silhouettes, and the inference that there is real, independent corroboration from others. We can see that the scene offers only his testimony and the absence of other witnesses, so there is no concrete evidence to support the claimed event beyond his statement.
captions.wrong-causal-direction: The image shows a cheerful man pointing at a distressed couple, who sit beneath a dark rain cloud with unpaid bills, a bottle, and a book labeled "Self Help" open between them. An arrow links the couple's troubled scene directly back to the book, implying that reading self-help materials is what caused their ongoing struggles and misfortune. The important contrast is between the visible evidence of the couple’s financial and emotional hardship and the suggestion that these problems are a result of reading self-help books. We can see stress, bills, and sadness, but nothing in the image itself proves that the books created the couple’s difficulties rather than the couple seeking the books because they were already struggling.
